name: When should I replace my kitchen floor instead of repairing it?

mainEntity.name: When should I replace my kitchen floor instead of repairing it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homeowners should consider replacing kitchen flooring when there is persistent water damage, deep subfloor softness, loose or cracked tiles, or extensive wear that cleaning cannot fix. In a busy kitchen, damaged floors can allow spills to seep into the subfloor, leading to mold or rot. A practical tradeoff to weigh is whether spot repairs make sense; while minor tile cracks can occasionally be patched, widespread issues or outdated layouts usually justify a full replacement to ensure a level, moisture-resistant base across your entire kitchen footprint.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replace your kitchen floor if you notice widespread water damage, soft subfloors, or loose tiles. Full replacement prevents moisture leaks and ensures a level base.
